`POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a
per-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is p
inned on the session's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved s
election carries, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.\n\nThe SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the sam
e operations:\n`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits the selection the target\nalready has, and is refused (`se

nd modelSelection`) when there is none.

## Not in the API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** availa

ble over the API
today (most exist in the hosted inspector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design; see [Authe
ntication](#authentication))\n* Chat and conformance suites\n* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth your

self,
 then upload the token to one of the server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Di

scord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z); it directly shapes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is *
*path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **Dur
ing the preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelo
g/overview.md).\n* **Additive changes** (new endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes) are
considered non-breaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.\n* Error **codes** are stable ident

ifiers; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `sce
nario` is\n**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the\noperation names, the SDK types and the n

oun-bearing response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects
/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/stud
ies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n
| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-ru
ns/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `
.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/

{swarmRunId}/insights` |

Response fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `s

warmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`ge
t_user_testing_scenario` served the environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-depend

ent fields are
absent rather than null when you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including
its old response\nspellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. The old paths ar

e not in the OpenAPI spec, and they are removed
at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the
rename and so have no\ndeprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm`

emit both and accept either, never both in
one request, until general availability.

### Vocabulary

Renamed field values can
not be aliased the way paths are, so they are chosen\nby header. Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read\nca

nonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `
parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `jour

neyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |
| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |

Abs
ent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may nam
e a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one. A response that varies by vo

cabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is
eval-
scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so read\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/c
apabilities` (`apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are\ntwo blocks) before sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …,

apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or
`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink resource types work differently: `st
udy` and\n`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and whic
h one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION rather than the header; a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprec

ated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.
